To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BlackBox scheduler is a systematic method for finding optimal thread assignments of multithread network applications running on multithreaded/multicore processors.

the BlackBox scheduler improves the system performance by up to 60% with respect to a baseline, and by up to 48% with respect to load-balancing algorithms used in state of the art OSs, with no data about the applications or the target architecture.
BlackBox scheduler is an optimal thread assignment method for multicore/multitheaded processors that requires minimum information about processor hardware and no data about applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of optimal thread assignment for multithreaded applications on multithreaded/multicore processors.
the development and evaluation of the BlackBox thread assignment method for multicore/multthreaded processors.
the development of a new thread assignment method that is capable of finding the best thread assignments in state-of-the art multicore/multitreaded processors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BlackBox thread assignment is the best choice for the studied applications, and it is also a very good choice in the majority of other applications, too.
BlackBox is an effective and efficient method that can improve the performance of multithread applications running on multicored/multithread processors.
the proposed thread assignment algorithm can be used as the default assignment algorithm for multithreaded applications running on multicor/multithread systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BlackBox is the first thread assignment method that is able to improve system performance without any knowledge about the target processor or the application under study.
the proposed method can be used as a basis for thread scheduling in future OSs.
the proposed method can be used to improve the system throughput by 10-50% with respect to the current state-of-the-art.
The main takeaway from our work is that

thread assignment can be a promising way to improve the performance of network applications on state-of-the-art multithreaded architectures, and that a thread assignment method with a minimum amount of information about the target architecture can provide a substantial performance improvement.

thread scheduling can have a significant impact on performance and that a thread scheduling algorithm that is aware of the hardware context requirements of the applications can significantly improve the system performance.

the performance of multithread applications can be significantly improved by assigning them to the processor hardware contexts using a systematic method that requires minimum data about the target processor and the applications under study.
